claims.statement: PPWR generally applies from 12 August 2026 and covers all packaging placed on the EU market.

A manufacturer must perform or commission the conformity assessment, compile technical documentation, draw up the declaration, and retain it for five years for single-use packaging or ten years for reusable packaging.

A brand owner can be the manufacturer when packaging or a packaged product is made under its own name, while suppliers must provide the manufacturer with necessary packaging information and documentation.

Several labelling, recycled-content, minimisation, and design-for-recycling methods are delivered through later implementing or delegated acts, creating both continuing update work and present uncertainty.

A low-cost native competitor already offers per-SKU technical files, declarations, converter positioning, component graphs, AI assistance, and ERP/API connectivity at EUR 29-299 per month before enterprise pricing.
Recyda directly covers supplier data, component relationships, APIs, audit trails, portfolio status, technical documentation, and declarations.
Specright has added PPWR declarations to an existing specification-management platform, while VINQ combines supplier collection and expert-validated packaging files.
Converters will choose and pay for a shared evidence exchange that their brand customers adopt alongside existing PLM systems.
Many-to-many reuse of converter evidence creates a defensible network effect not available from incumbent supplier portals and APIs.

contrary_evidence: PPWR Connect offers broad functionality at EUR 29-299 per month and already targets converters.
Recyda offers nearly the full proposed evidence graph, API, audit, and declaration workflow to enterprise customers.
Specright embeds PPWR into incumbent packaging specification management and already has supplier collection.
VINQ includes human expert validation, weakening a managed-service differentiator.
The brand or other legal manufacturer remains responsible for the declaration, limiting a converter's control point.
Later implementing acts delay or change parts of the detailed requirement set.
